questions.q: Why is the Gupta era called a 'Golden Age' of Indian culture?
answer: The Gupta era, from about 320 to 550 CE, is called a Golden or Classical Age because of its outstanding achievements in many fields.

answer.text: Sanskrit literature reached great heights, above all in the works of Kalidasa, such as the play Abhijnana-shakuntalam and the poem Meghaduta.

This age used the decimal system and the concept of zero. Aryabhata argued that the Earth rotates on its axis and worked on the value of pi and the cause of eclipses, while Varahamihira advanced astronomy and Sushruta and Charaka developed medicine and surgery.
Temple architecture developed, and the finest paintings of the age adorn the Ajanta caves. Such wide creativity earns the era its title.

questions.q: Describe the achievements of Samudragupta and Chandragupta II.

answer.text: Samudragupta was a great conqueror who extended Gupta power over much of India. His campaigns and qualities are recorded in the Prayaga Prashasti, the Allahabad Pillar inscription composed by his court poet Harishena.

Chandragupta II, who took the title Vikramaditya, defeated the Shakas of western India and brought the empire to its height. The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign and left an account of a prosperous, well-governed land.
Under these two rulers the Guptas reached their greatest extent and ushered in the cultural flowering of the classical age.
